answer: Sybils thus burn capital and time per fake node, making mass duplication economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a slow comet that only passes the oasis registry once per cycle, and that bond acts as an anchor: peers verify the comet's signed passage, so forging a new identity costs a full re-stake plus a cycle of waiting. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
